newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securitas to expand in France.
newsitem.headline: Securitas to expand in France.

text.p: Swedish security company Securitas AB said on Tuesday it signed an agreement with Groupe Consortium de Realisation (CDR) to take over SGI Surveillance's French operations.
"This acquisiton is a major complement to Securitas's market coverage in France," the company said in a statement.
The acquisition is conditioned on approval by the French Finance ministry, which is expected in February.
SGI Surveillance has 2,400 employees and in 1996 its annual sales amounted to 420 million crowns, Securitas said.
The acquisition will not affect Securitas 1997 earnings, the company said.
Securitas said it had also bought three small alarm operations in the Paris region, JLMT SA, Telesurveillance SARL and CTGM SARL with combined 1996 sales of around 18 million crowns.
"These acquisitions will strengthen the current installation and maintenance business of Securitas in the Paris region," the company said.
In 1997, the company's total French sales will be around one billion crowns, Securitas said.
